description: Export material keys (measurements.json `materials`, shared/README.md) -> hand-made Unreal materials (#2282). tools/unreal-engine/python/import_world.py replaces every imported material instance whose key matches a rule (first match wins, Python regex on the key; an optional `mesh` regex also has to match the StaticMesh asset name, which is the id of the first export node using that mesh). Keys that match no rule keep Interchange's glTF material instance, which carries the key's colour, roughness, metalness, opacity and emissive. tools/unreal-engine/python/build_materials.py builds every entry under `materials` (masters first, then instances). `scope` and `defaults` drive the key-coverage check in tools/unreal-engine/tests/test_materials.py: every key on a building or ground node of the export must match a rule or a default with a reason. `source` names where the web takes the look from; `assumption` carries plan-material's *guess* markers into the asset metadata (Lunden.Source / Lunden.Assumption).

scope.note: Building and ground surfaces: every export node that is not furniture, interactive, light, collision or fixture. The `structure` kind also holds fixed fittings (kitchen, bathroom, radiators, vents, curtains); their keys are covered by rules or explicit defaults too.

vertexColor.note: #2321: Interchange's glTF masters multiply COLOR_0 only in their base-colour-texture branch (static switch bHasBaseColorTexture), so an untextured vertex-coloured key (`_vc`: three.js vertexColors, the export keeps the colour attribute) with a white or light base colour came out white. After the rules, import_world.py re-parents every imported instance whose key matches `match` and that has no base colour texture from its Interchange master onto the listed project copy (the instance keeps its parameters and its parent chain's blend/two-sided overrides). An unlisted master fails the import; tests/test_materials.py fails when an export key with vertex colours would get a master without vertex colour, in any zone.

defaults.reason: patio hedge and boxwood (#2325): the textured Interchange branch multiplies the leaf map and clump shading by the vertex colour (#2321). The pilot planting uses the patio material by its original path
exterior image from the GLB: slat cut-out or letter atlas (#2325); keep its Interchange material instance

transparent fittings (front-door glazing, shower screen, glass shelf, curtains): Interchange's translucent instance keeps tint and opacity; textiles are #2289; those meshes use the raster path (#2276)
emissive fittings (lamp shades, mirror, displays, night light): Interchange's instance keeps the emissive colour; lamps and light belong to #2283

textured fittings that are not building or ground surfaces (kitchen worktop, door name plate, picture prints): the web's canvas texture does not travel, the Interchange instance keeps its base colour; furnishing looks are #2289

vertex-coloured fittings (door handles, vents, frames, plant pots, plants): the imported instance keeps colour, roughness and metalness on a master that multiplies the vertex colour in (`vertexColor`, #2321); fittings, not surfaces

plain opaque PBR fitting (kitchen and bathroom fronts, steel, sanitary ware, radiators, sills, appliances): the key's colour, roughness and metalness are the whole web material, which Interchange's instance reproduces
